QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_7

question.text: During an LP marketing roadshow, the CIO of Kailash Capital AIF is asked to quote the current size of the Indian AIF industry. Per the figures cited in Chapter 3 of the NISM XIX-D workbook, as of December 31, 2025, the CUMULATIVE capital commitments raised by all SEBI-registered AIFs (across all three categories) have surpassed approximately what level?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.5 'Current AIF Market in India' states that capital commitments raised by all registered AIFs (across categories) have surpassed INR 15.74 lakh crore as on December 31, 2025. The chapter also notes 1,771 AIFs were registered with SEBI as on February 11, 2026, up from just 21 funds in 2012. The Trap: INR 1.57 lakh crore understates the market by an order of magnitude. INR 5.74 lakh crore is an older figure that has been exceeded. INR 157 lakh crore overstates by 10x and would exceed the entire Indian mutual fund AUM — a red-flag distractor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XIX-C use the same AIF-market-size statistic. For MF comparison, XXI-A and X-A cite the MF industry AUM separately. Numbers are updated each workbook revision — memorize the most recent figure. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching to a global pension LP, always present the AIF industry commitments figure alongside 'drawn capital' (typically 60-65% of commitments) — commitments alone overstate deployed AUM, and sophisticated LPs will ask you to bridge commitment vs. drawn on slide 1.
